analysis.title: Analog Devices Inc. (ADI): 4Q Preview: Cyclical recovery and datacenter momentum to drive solid quarter; supply flexibility in focus
key_insights: GS expects a solid FY4Q26 with revenue guidance above the Street. Investors are likely to focus on the industrial recovery, datacenter trends and supply flexibility.
GS describes investor positioning as balanced. Analog peers gave constructive commentary on key end markets, set against challenges on capacity and input costs.
GS expects ADI fundamentals to track just ahead of peers on idiosyncratic drivers. It says ADI could flag similar supply challenges given its hybrid manufacturing model.
GS expects 1Q27 guidance of flat to low-single-digit revenue decline on typical seasonality, partly offset by strength in communications (datacenter).
GS expects upside to the Street at the high end of guidance. Its FY27 non-GAAP EPS estimate is about 2% above the Street on industrial strength and idiosyncratic growth drivers.

Three call items could move the stock: industrial and automotive demand commentary, datacenter momentum exiting 2026, and supply flexibility and margins. GS cites potential gross margin levers into FY27 from higher pricing versus input costs.
GS says investor expectations are elevated after generally strong analog peer reports, but positioning is more balanced after the recent sector selloff.

GS thinks the stock can move higher on a solid quarter. The debate after the print should continue on end-market demand, with more near-term upside if management signals confidence in supply flexibility and margins.

market_movers.rationale: 12-month target of $480 is based on 32X P/E applied to normalized EPS of $15.00. The stock closed at $394.66 on 9 Nov 2026, implying 21.6% upside.

sector_views.rationale: GS expects constructive industrial recovery and datacenter momentum for ADI. Supply and input cost challenges at peers are the main watch item.

earnings_insights: ADI FY4Q26E (GS estimate): revenue $4,380mn vs Street $4,326mn (+1.2%). EPS incl. SBC $4.00 vs Street $3.90 (+2.5%). Operating margin 52.9% vs Street 52.2%. These are estimates ahead of the print, not reported figures.
ADI FY1Q27E (GS estimate): revenue $4,352mn vs Street $4,332mn (+0.5%). EPS incl. SBC $3.94 vs Street $3.87 (+1.9%). Operating margin 52.4% vs Street 51.5%.
ADI FY2026E (GS estimate): revenue $15,185mn vs Street $15,132mn (+0.4%). EPS incl. SBC $13.00 vs Street $12.89 (+0.8%).
ADI FY2027E (GS estimate): revenue $18,502mn vs Street $18,500mn (0.0%). EPS incl. SBC $17.20 vs Street $16.83 (+2.2%). The cover text says FY27 non-GAAP EPS is about 2% above the Street.
ADI FY2028E (GS estimate): revenue $21,312mn vs Street $20,427mn (+4.3%). EPS incl. SBC $21.00 vs Street $19.43 (+8.1%). Industrial revenue is $11,101mn vs Street $10,081mn (+10.1%).

FY4Q26E segment revenue (GS vs Street, estimates): Automotive $1,038mn vs $1,028mn, Industrial $2,169mn vs $2,144mn, Communications $740mn vs $726mn, Consumer $433mn vs $428mn. Total revenue growth is 42.4% y/y for GS and 37.7% for the Street.
risk_factors: Lack of share gains in the auto or industrial end market.
Increased competition in China could drive price pressure.
Lack of demand reversal in analog.
ADI could flag supply challenges given its hybrid manufacturing model, as some analog peers did on capacity and input costs.
vol_and_positioning: GS says positioning in ADI is likely more balanced given the recent sector selloff, despite elevated expectations after strong analog peer reports.
